claim: dbbi (91) parsed left-to-right with b and g as two-character prefixes gives exactly 64 tokens with exactly 16 distinct codes (a ba bb be bf bh c d e f gb ge gg gi h i). The claim is that it could be a substituted SHA-256 hex digest. The equality pattern (labels by first occurrence) is 01234556728966286abc61c88b48de3086dd501d5557d6bab5605233df7bbb96. b/g is said to be the only prefix pair of 36 that gives 64/16; shuffle control 0.3% (post hoc).
method: prefix-parse; compare isomorphism pattern of sha256(candidate) hex
self_verifying_note: If any candidate's sha256 hex has the same 64-position equality pattern, that is ~impossible by chance, so the mapping recovers itself. It works as a judge for matrixsumlist serializations. The 64/16 parse count was reproduced here.
status: open; overlaps our b/be prime-position finding
novelty: medium (pattern-match harness is new to us)
